purpose: A metric-blind intake ledger for possible v3 benchmark cases. This file is not a benchmark result and its counts do not contribute to readiness.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), replication catalog and 1960-1985 time window
Swanson (1986), Fish oil, Raynaud's syndrome, and undiscovered public knowledge
Gordon and Lindsay (1996), independent replication and re-examination
DiGiacomo et al. (1989), double-blind controlled prospective study

adjudication.rationale: Canonical development diagnostic with a documented pre-discovery window, later bridge publication, independent LBD replication, and subsequent clinical study. Historical MeSH remains unavailable, so it is not eligible as a period-appropriate held-out case.

evidence.label: Swanson (1988), Migraine and magnesium: eleven neglected connections
Weeber et al. (2001), concept-based simulation of both Swanson discoveries

adjudication.rationale: Canonical development diagnostic with a bridge publication and independent concept-based replication. Historical MeSH remains unavailable, so it is not eligible as a period-appropriate held-out case.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), one of seven literature replication cases

open_questions: Adjudicate the exact cutoff independently of the published evaluation window.
Audit both concepts against the intended vocabulary release.
Find independent evidence that the relationship qualifies as a discovery rather than only an LBD replication target.

adjudication.rationale: A frequently reused replication case is only a candidate until its cutoff, mapping, and discovery status are independently adjudicated.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), one of seven literature replication cases

open_questions: Locate a stable primary-publication record for the 1994 bridge paper.
Adjudicate the cutoff independently of the published evaluation window.
Resolve the broad neurologic-disease concept to a period-appropriate descriptor.

adjudication.rationale: The replication catalog is sufficient for intake, not for positive-case acceptance.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), one of seven literature replication cases
Smalheiser and Swanson (1996), Indomethacin and Alzheimer's disease

open_questions: Adjudicate whether this is a discovery case when direct pre-window connections are reported.
Define a cutoff that precedes the bridge publication.
Audit both concepts against the intended vocabulary release.

adjudication.rationale: The catalog reports six direct connections in its evaluation segment, so novelty cannot be assumed from reuse as an LBD case.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), one of seven literature replication cases
Smalheiser and Swanson (1996), Linking estrogen to Alzheimer's disease

open_questions: Adjudicate whether this is a discovery case when direct pre-window connections are reported.
Pin the pre-publication cutoff and vocabulary release.
Find an independent assessment of the claimed discovery.

adjudication.rationale: The catalog reports 25 direct connections in its evaluation segment; this may be hypothesis organization rather than a previously absent relation.

evidence.label: Preiss and Stevenson (2017), one of seven literature replication cases
Smalheiser and Swanson (1998), Calcium-independent phospholipase A2 and schizophrenia

open_questions: Resolve the source's inconsistent 1997/1998 publication dating before fixing a cutoff.
Audit the enzyme concept against the intended vocabulary release.
Find an independent assessment of the claimed discovery.

adjudication.rationale: The stable PubMed record dates the bridge to 1998 while secondary replication literature sometimes labels it 1997; the case cannot be frozen with an unresolved cutoff.

evidence.label: Moreau (2023), example of a chance co-occurrence mislabelled by time-sliced evaluation

adjudication.rationale: A later co-occurrence alone is not evidence of a meaningful discovery. This pair is retained only as an audit example of noisy timeslice labels.

evidence.label: Moreau (2023), example involving a generic term mislabelled by time-sliced evaluation

adjudication.rationale: A generic population term newly co-occurring with a disease is not by itself a discovery. This pair is retained only as a benchmark-construction warning.
